gaps.quote: Each source, gate and sink $\nu$ carries an invertible linear operator
gaps.note: The page never says what a source, gate, sink, node, edge or route of the network is (a wire's first vertex, a linear map on several wires, its last vertex, a segment between consecutive vertices). The reader has only 'a fixed wiring of linear steps'.

gaps.quote: By the telescoping, the route applies $\varepsilon_w D_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$
gaps.note: The result needs the supplied physical input f to be read as the logical array D_in^{-1} f (the paper, lines 141-142 and 794-805, defines this); the page never says how the input is interpreted, so the factor D_source(w)^{-1} appears without justification.

gaps.quote: Take an input role $w$ and its route to output role $\rho(w)$, carrying sign $\varepsilon_w \in \{+1,-1\}$.
gaps.note: Gates combine several wires, so a single route with a sign is not defined for an arbitrary network. It holds only because the scalar network as a whole is a signed permutation of roles; the paper (lines 816-823) derives the route formula from the whole-network identity D_out S D_in^{-1}, which the page never states. The page does not say the scalar network is a signed role permutation.
